notes.summary: The participant says the supplied procedure describes current work. It documents arrangement setup, reconciliation, fee and eligibility checks, deemed contributions, capital events, special profits, departures and period close; the initiating event and overall accountable role remain unclear.

topics.answer: The work is named Deemed Contributions, Fee Waivers & Special Profits; the procedure uses FA-06.
The documented work maintains member-level deemed contributions and commitment balances and produces a reconciled, approved period or event package.

The arrangement requires governing documents, client approval and member/commitment data before starting. Departure or loss of eligibility is a separate documented condition for restructuring.
The initiating notification for establishing an arrangement, its sender, cadence and deadlines are not established by the supplied procedure.

The preparer and second reviewer reconcile opening plus current deemed contributions to ending ICC by member, commitments to their funding components, fee and event treatment, capital accounts and GL, and member schedules to GP records. They confirm special-profits support, lock and distribute the approved source schedule, and retain approvals and unresolved-item ownership. The period/event remains open for unresolved schedule or accounting divergence; one approved life-to-date version and zero unexplained differences are required.
The procedure names preparers and reviewers but does not identify the role accountable for the overall result.

The assigned Fund Administration preparer, with client/advisor input, identifies the fund, GP vehicle, eligible members, effective date and affected fees; records the method and cash- and waiver-funded commitment components by member; obtains written client and advisor confirmation; and designates the controlled life-to-date schedule. The outputs are an approved arrangement record and opening schedule.
The Fund Administration preparer rolls forward prior waived fees and deemed contributions by member, reconciles commitment components to GP records and cumulative contributions and special profits to capital accounts and GL/TB, and identifies duplicate, omitted or divergent balances. A second reviewer verifies; differences are resolved or documented before new activity, and version divergence is escalated.
The preparer, with client confirmation, checks member eligibility as of the fee/event date against current status and the prior population. Departures, leave, exceptions and changed elections are identified; new waiver activity for an ineligible member is suspended pending approved restructuring, with departures and exceptions routed to the departure step.
The management-fee preparer provides the approved period/event calculation and the receiving preparer validates gross fee, offsets, waiver, net fee and member allocation, including period, entity, dates and version. The waiver is checked against the arrangement and cumulative tracking; unexplained differences are returned for resolution.
Using the approved waived fee and eligible population, the preparer calculates each member's deemed contribution under the governing arrangement, adds it to the life-to-date ICC roll-forward, reduces applicable waiver-funded unfunded commitment as approved, and updates capital-account and accounting support. Accounting/Fund Team posts as applicable; cash and waiver components remain separately visible.
For a capital event, the preparer coordinates with the event preparer, separates each member's waiver-funded amount from cash due, updates allocation and notice data, and reconciles event results to the ICC and GP unfunded schedules. Cash due plus waiver funding must equal the approved allocation; unclear treatment or disclosure is escalated to the client/advisor.
The preparer establishes the special-profits method, timing, available-income definition, population and target adjustment with client tax/legal advisor and client approval, and checks the period/event condition. Written advisor and client approval is required before calculation or accounting entry; if the method is unspecified, the work is held for advisor direction.
The preparer calculates and allocates special profits under the approved method, updates capital-account schedules and outputs, and reconciles allocations and recorded amounts to the approved total. A second reviewer checks and accounting/Fund Team posts; negative, excessive or unsupported results are escalated to client/advisors.
On departure or loss of eligibility, the procedure calls for stopping new waiver funding from the effective date unless written client/advisor direction says otherwise. Treatment is determined with the client, including possible cash conversion, forfeiture or partner reallocation; the preparer updates affected schedules and reconciles the before/after structure. Replacement or forfeiture must not be assumed.

The arrangement check requires support for every member, amount source, method and effective date; missing governing terms or advisor approval holds calculation. Opening balances require zero unexplained differences across the designated roll-forward, GP schedule, capital accounts and accounting.
No deemed contribution is recorded for an ineligible period/member without written advisor/client direction. Special-profits allocations must equal the approved total, satisfy available-income and capital-account limits, and have no unexplained residual.

The documented arrangement may use an LPA-dictated, fixed-schedule or waive-first-then-true-up method. Departure treatment may involve cash conversion, forfeiture or reallocation, subject to client/advisor direction rather than assumption.
The procedure warns that unclear status source, responsible role or timing can allow an ineligible waiver to continue or a commitment to be allocated incorrectly.

The supplied FA-06 procedure documents the steps. Its working and retained records include the arrangement summary, ICC/waiver roll-forward, GP capital and commitment schedules, fee workpapers, member-status and change records, approved fee input, special-profits methodology and available-income schedules, GL support and the approved period/event package.
The participant says the supplied procedure describes how the work is done today and has nothing to add. The detailed steps below are documented procedure, not independently verified observations.

The documented special-profits gate uses the LPA/side agreements, approved method, capital accounts and available-income support. A supported method, available-income result and approval are required before a shift. A workbook, template, prior deliverable or recollection is not independent authority unless the source explicitly establishes an approved policy.
The available procedure does not specify the special-profits formula or method, nor the deemed-contribution accounting entry and exact offsets; it directs staff to obtain advisor or approved accounting direction.

The process consumes an approved management-fee calculation supplied by the management-fee preparer, coordinates with the capital-event preparer, and distributes its approved schedule to dependent processes. The supplied extraction does not bind every distribution recipient to a named process.

The procedure designates a controlled life-to-date ICC/waiver roll-forward and uses fee workpapers, GP schedules, a capital-call workbook, capital accounts and GL/TB for inputs and reconciliation. It calls for locking one approved current version.
